steps.title: Write the rules for your agents (AGENTS.md)
steps.why: an agent follows the rules it can read, and only those

steps.title: Turn on the guard for your agents' commands
steps.why: the guard stops a risky command, like a force push, before the agent runs it

steps.title: Check each commit before it is made
steps.why: a secret or a personal email is hard to take back once a commit is pushed

steps.title: Add the yokoten runtime to the project
steps.why: the hooks and CI run this copy, so they work with no network and no global install

steps.title: Run your tests on every push
steps.why: tests that run on every push catch a broken change before it reaches main

steps.title: Put the project on GitHub or Gitea
steps.why: the code host keeps a copy, so a lost machine does not lose the work

steps.title: Run the checks on every pull request
steps.why: a commit made with the hook off would reach main unchecked

steps.title: Turn on issues
steps.why: an issue has an owner, a state and a history; a todo file has none

steps.title: Add issue and pull request templates
steps.why: a template asks for what a reviewer needs, so nothing is forgotten

steps.title: Add the standard labels
steps.why: a label says what kind of change a pull request is, and the pull request check asks for one

steps.title: Add a first milestone
steps.why: a milestone says when a change ships, and the pull request check asks for one

steps.title: Keep build output out of git
steps.why: a build makes these files again from the source, and a reviewer can't read a binary

steps.title: Keep a changelog
steps.why: each pull request adds its entry as it goes, so a release needs no digging

steps.title: Check pull request titles
steps.why: a pull request title becomes the commit on main, so it must say what changed and why

steps.title: Name the owner (CODEOWNERS)
steps.why: the host then asks you to review a pull request that changes those paths, and `check --pr` makes it tier A

steps.title: Set up the bot account
steps.why: when the bot opens pull requests, you review work you did not write, as a team does

steps.title: Install the yokoten skills
steps.why: the skills show an agent how to hand off work, review it and find the cause of a failure

steps.title: Keep your agents in a sandbox
steps.why: a worker writes only where the sandbox allows, so it must cover the worktree

steps.title: Ask for a review before a merge
steps.why: the bot opens the pull requests, so you approve work you did not write, and nothing merges unread

steps.title: Add a license and a security policy
steps.why: people can then report a hole in private, old dependencies get updates, and others know how they may use the code

steps.title: Protect the main branch
steps.why: the guards catch an agent's mistakes, but only the server stops a push that gets past them

steps.title: Set the merge settings
steps.why: one pull request becomes one commit on main, and no merged branch is left behind

steps.title: Turn on the security settings
steps.why: the host then stops a pushed secret, and people can report a hole in private

steps.title: Let only you create release tags
steps.why: a tag that nobody can push blocks a release, and a bot on the list can push one

steps.title: Approve each release yourself
steps.why: without it, a publish job that a tag starts runs without anyone approving it

steps.title: Limit releases to version tags
steps.why: a branch rule named v* matches no tag, and with both rules a branch named v* can still publish
